posts.title: What to bring to a first consultation
posts.excerpt: A structured checklist of medical records, current medications, and fasting blood test details to help you prepare for your initial 60-minute visit at Hisui Clinic.
posts.content:
Attending a first medical consultation for an endocrine condition often comes after months of uncertainty, changing symptoms, or inconclusive routine tests. At Hisui Clinic, our founding principle since 2011 has been to replace fragmented healthcare with unhurried continuity. Your initial consultation lasts a full 60 minutes with your assigned endocrinologist—Helena Varga for diabetes care, Tomas Okafor for thyroid and pituitary conditions, or Mei Lindgren for life-stage hormone transitions. Because we dedicate this time to building a complete clinical picture, arriving prepared ensures that your appointment addresses your health thoroughly without missing essential history.

Bring your laboratory records

The foundation of any meaningful endocrine evaluation is accurate laboratory data. When you arrange your appointment with our patient coordinator, Claire Mbeki, she will schedule your fasting blood tests between 08:00 and 10:00 on the morning of your consultation. Having your blood drawn in our third-floor phlebotomy bay during this specific two-hour window allows our partner laboratory to process fasting glucose, insulin, and hormone profiles in time for your afternoon review. Please remember to fast from midnight before your blood draw, drinking only water, and bring along copies of any blood tests, ultrasound scans, or diagnostic reports completed by other clinics during the preceding twelve months.

Bring your medicines and readings

Bringing an exact record of your current medications and supplements is equally vital. Rather than attempting to recall dosages from memory, we ask that you bring your actual prescription packaging or a complete written summary detailing exact strengths and schedules. This includes oral tablets, insulin types, hormone replacement therapies, over-the-counter vitamins, and herbal supplements. For patients managing diabetes, having your recent blood glucose logs, paper diaries, or continuous glucose monitor sensor data ready for review allows your physician to evaluate trends rather than isolated numbers.

We also encourage you to bring a written list of your primary daily symptoms and lifestyle observations. Endocrine conditions affect everyday energy, sleep quality, weight stability, and temperature tolerance, and these subtle patterns are easily overlooked in the moment. Noting when symptoms typically appear, how they relate to meals or physical activity, and what questions you hope to resolve gives your doctor valuable context. If you work rotating shifts or have irregular eating schedules, writing down a typical weekday routine helps us tailor medical decisions to your real life.

After the consultation: your written plan

Following your 60-minute discussion, your endocrinologist will not leave you with unwritten impressions or vague directions. Within 7 days, your doctor formulates an agreed one-page written plan that both you and your physician sign. This document records your confirmed regimen, medication timing, dietary guidelines developed with dietitian Jonas Reiter where appropriate, and a clear timeline for your next 40-minute plan review in 3 months. Between visits, our dedicated nurse line, staffed by Rosa Almeida and Priya Nair, is available Monday through Friday from 09:00 to 17:00 to answer questions within one working day.

Taking time to gather your records, prepare your medication list, and attend your morning blood test between 08:00 and 10:00 sets the stage for a calm and productive first appointment. At 3F, 42 Alder Quay, our clinical team is here to listen, investigate thoroughly, and establish a clear care plan that supports your health over years.

posts.title: Fasting blood tests: the 08:00–10:00 window
posts.excerpt: Why early-morning blood draws give an accurate baseline for thyroid panels and metabolic profiles discussed the same day.
posts.content:
Fasting tests are drawn at the clinic between 08:00 and 10:00 on weekdays. Water is fine; food and sweet drinks are not.

Because the sample is taken in the morning, your doctor can discuss the result with you the same day rather than days later.

posts.title: Sensor start sessions now on Saturdays
posts.excerpt: We have added Saturday appointments with our diabetes nurse educators for sensor fitting and a practical walk-through.
posts.content:
Sensor start sessions last 45 minutes and cost €70. A nurse educator fits the sensor, sets up the reader and shows you how to read the trace.

Saturday sessions run between 08:30 and 12:30. Book through the patient coordinator.

posts.title: Direct referral pathways and shared care
posts.excerpt: How community physicians can coordinate with our endocrinologists on diabetes, thyroid ultrasound follow-up and shared obstetric care.
posts.content:
Referring clinicians can send a short letter with recent results to hello@hisui-clinic.example. The patient coordinator calls the patient within one working day.

We send the written plan back to the referring clinician once it is agreed with the patient.
